import csv
from collections import defaultdict
rows=list(csv.DictReader(open(VALUES_CSV)))
ts=sorted(set(r['timestamp'] for r in rows))
data=defaultdict(dict)
for r in rows:
    data[r['timeseries_id']][r['timestamp']]=float(r['value'])
ids={'Zone_F1_Z01': '7a9e6dea-7214-57d7-a3ab-6fec741ab22a',
'Zone_F2_Z01':'baef86cb-2941-5d61-87b0-ffa91d79f23a',
'Zone_F3_Z01':'e0dd5f44-f050-5faa-a2a0-a3fcb6284ae8',
'Zone_F4_Z01':'14a08406-79a0-52ca-b8a1-8563259dc820'}
def avg(id, lo, hi):
    vals=[data[id][t] for t in ts if lo<=t<=hi and t in data[id]]
    return sum(vals)/len(vals) if vals else None
for name,id in ids.items():
    a=sum(val for t,val in data[id].items() if t<'2018-07-01')/len([t for t in data[id] if t<'2018-07-01'])
    b=sum(val for t,val in data[id].items() if t>='2018-07-01')/len([t for t in data[id] if t>='2018-07-01'])
    print(name, 'pre', round(a,2), 'post', round(b,2), 'diff', round(b-a,2))

content.text: The zone F3 sensor jumped ~2.0 °C in July 2018, but every other zone is stable. To distinguish "local load change" vs "sensor fault", we need an independent reading (e.g., supply-air flow/damper/valve commands, zone power draw, occupancy, outdoor air temp, or a redundant zone temperature sensor). The catalog only contains zone temperature sensors and setpoints — no independent load or control-effort signal, and no redundant temperature reference. So the two hypotheses are indistinguishable with available streams.
